Definition: neuter of the (irregular) comparative of G2570; (adverbially) better than many:--very well.
BiblicalUsage: Kallion is 'better' — the comparative of good, used here as an adverb. Paul tells Festus he has done the Jews no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Paul's 'very well' is the quiet confidence of a clear conscience: the truth is known, and it needs no embellishment.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
